title: Anthropometric and cardio-metabolic trait variation and genetic associations in sub-Saharan Africa.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI (National Center for Biotechnology Information) links, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. Europe PMC lists full text as 'Subscription required'. A dbGaP (NIH controlled-access genotype database) search for 'Tishkoff Africa' returns the lab's African genotype studies, e.g. phs001780.v1.p1, all controlled access.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: 2,124 individuals, 27 traits, dense genotypes, GWAS (genome-wide association study) with >100 significant SNPs (single-letter DNA variants). I could not read the data availability statement, so where the per-person data are deposited is inferred from the lab's earlier deposits, not confirmed.

a1_downloadable.note: No open files found. Per-person genotypes and phenotypes from African cohorts in this lab's past work sit in dbGaP, which needs an access application. The paper is paywalled, so I could not confirm its data statement. Flagged as controlled access.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. Measured traits (height, hemoglobin and others) would be columns per person, going by the abstract.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; genotypes described in the abstract only.

a5_enough_rows.note: 2,124 individuals per the abstract; not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checked; genotype-array data for about 2k people would likely fit.

a8_label_provenance.note: Traits are physical measurements per the abstract; not verified.

honest_claim_h3: Not reached; the data is not openly downloadable.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genetic ancestry and genotypes of sub-Saharan Africans to predict height and blood biomarker levels.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotypes and ancestry fractions for each person; about 2,124 people per the abstract (unverified).
plain_idea.predict: Measured traits such as height or hemoglobin, recorded in the field by the study team.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Shows whether trait prediction for Africans needs African training data instead of European-derived scores.

ml_idea: Predict traits from genotypes plus ancestry fractions, and compare against European polygenic scores. Blocked by controlled access to the per-person data.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the paper's data availability statement to see whether per-person phenotypes are open anywhere; most likely they are dbGaP/EGA only.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the paper is paywalled and has no open supplement or repository links. The per-person genotype and trait data are most likely controlled access (dbGaP, NIH's genotype database), which needs an application. Flagged as controlled access, which could take weeks to obtain.
